newsitem.title: CANADA: CBRS expects no change in Gulf ratings.
newsitem.headline: CBRS expects no change in Gulf ratings.

text.p: Canadian Bond Rating Service said on Wednesday it expected no changes to its Gulf Canada Resources Ltd debt ratings following a review of Gulf's bid for CS Resources Ltd.
CBRS said its reaffirmation reflected the modest amount of financing needed for Gulf to acquire CS, which has posted increases in operating and financial results through most of its history.
Gulf plans to offer either C$14.50 cash, subject to a maximum of C$100 million, or 1.1539 of a Gulf share for each CS share in a C$413 million deal.
If the offer is successful, there would be minimal impact on Gulf's debt capitalization because CS had only C$31.5 million in long-term debt compared to Gulf's C$2.6 billion, CBRS said.
Also, 76 percent of the deal was expected to be financed with Gulf equity, but if it was drawn into a bidding war, Gulf ratings would be reviewed again, CBRS said.
CBRS rates Gulf's commercial paper at A-2 (low), senior debentures and notes at B+ (high), senior subordinated debentures at B+ (low) and preferred shares at P-4.
It maintains a positive outlook on all the rated securities. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
